identity.fantasy: A vampiric blood caster who spends health to seed suffering, builds Thirst through repeated ruptures, and cashes the bank into curses, eruptions, parasites, or a Blood Lord transformation.
identity.one_line: A blood-and-Shadow caster that layers Transgression, diseases, blood eruptions, parasites, and vampiric cooldowns. It leeches and harvests essence while building toward Blood Lord and sacrificial burst windows, giving it strong sustain but substantial DoT and proc tracking.

mechanics.core_loop: Apply Transgression, build Thirst with the appropriate single-target or AoE generator, begin the dump near seven stacks so multi-cast payoffs land around ten, use Vampiric Fang to reset or harvest the sequence, and align Blood Lord or Sacrificial Rite with targets that will survive the ramp.
mechanics.single_target: Current players describe Transgression into Bloodmoon Blast stacks, Bloodbolt and Malediction setup, repeated Valanar's Vengeance, then Vampiric Fang after the final hit connects.
mechanics.aoe: Recent guidance builds roughly seven Thirst with Rupture, casts Keleseth's Calamity repeatedly, adds Atherann's Anguish when available, then uses Rupture and Vampiric Fang to reset; later cursed ground and parasites deepen the pack package.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Long effects and delayed projectiles punish rapid target turnover, while hard casts and health costs make forced movement more expensive than on a mobile weapon spec.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Vampiric Fang, Lifedrinker, Blood Banquet, Blood Cocoon, and later leech or lord effects return health, but the caster is deliberately spending the same health pool opponents attack.
mechanics.group_utility: Fear, control, and Bloodmage off-healing remain available, though the specialization's distinctive group tension is managing self-damage without creating avoidable healer load.

failure_modes.text: Sitting at maximum Thirst or mistiming Vampiric Fang wastes the ramp; in PvP, health-cost casts can make the caster easier to kill before the payoff lands.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: long effects and delayed projectiles punish rapid target turnover, while hard casts and health costs make forced movement more expensive than on a mobile weapon spec.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: vampiric fang, lifedrinker, blood banquet, blood cocoon, and later leech or lord effects return health, but the caster is deliberately spending the same health pool opponents attack.

enjoy_if.text: You enjoy deliberate ramp sequences where health, stacks, delayed hits, and a transformation payoff all interact.

You enjoy the spec's core cadence: apply transgression, build thirst with the appropriate single-target or aoe generator, begin the dump near seven stacks so multi-cast payoffs land around ten, use vampiric fang to reset or harvest the sequence, and align blood lord or sacrificial rite with targets that will survive the ramp.

avoid_if.text: You dislike self-damage, long setup, or depending on a target living until delayed effects finish.

You dislike the positioning or swap constraint that long effects and delayed projectiles punish rapid target turnover, while hard casts and health costs make forced movement more expensive than on a mobile weapon spec.

praise.theme: Players call the fantasy and ramp loop fun, and current rotation advice reports strong later-level AoE when Thirst is dumped correctly.

frustrations.theme: Recent PvP players describe extreme self-damage, weak compensation, hard-cast vulnerability, and unwanted healer pressure.

contested.theme: The spec has a documented functioning PvE rotation and moderate DPS signal while current PvP sentiment calls it effectively unplayable; those contexts must remain separate.

append_claims.text: A July 30 Bloodmage leveling discussion says the class begins functioning better around level 20 when Stamina and Spirit scaling arrive; Sanguine players specifically praise the talent making Bloodbolt critically interact with Transgression and the resulting healing.

A current Sanguine discussion describes building about seven Thirst before a multi-cast dump, then timing Vampiric Fang after the final payoff lands. For AoE it proposes Rupture into repeated Keleseth's Calamity, with Atherann's Anguish before the dump when available.

A July 31 PvP report describes Sanguine as a fun ramping health-cost caster but argues its self-damage, hard casts, and insufficient sustained recovery make it extremely weak in PvP; replies broadly agree while noting context dependence with dedicated healing.
append_claims.notes: Strong mode-specific sentiment, not a PvE conclusion.

append_claims.text: The July community DPS compilation reports Sanguine at 4,315, and the August Mythic inventory lists 67 Sanguine records.
append_claims.notes: PvE signal cannot resolve the PvP complaint; methodology and sample composition remain incomplete.

append_claims.text: Sanguine pays a compounded penalty when a target dies, moves, or disrupts the caster before delayed effects and the Thirst reset complete, because both setup time and self-health were already spent.
append_claims.notes: Magnitude varies by target lifetime and build.
